findings.issue_text: [BUG] enableSqlExpressions returns false on every code path, so the SQL expression gate can never open. Every frontend expression of type QueryTypeSQL is rejected with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" at line 129-131, regardless of the FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle setting — the feature is permanently dead and any dashboard using SQL expressions returns errors after deploy.

[BUG] The new code references featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions but the diff adds no featuremgmt import to reader.go, so the package does not compile. `go build ./pkg/expr` fails with "undefined: featuremgmt" (or an unresolved import) — CI and all downstream builds break; nothing in this diff ships until the import is added.

[BUG] Execute now calls sql.NewInMemoryDB() but the diff's import hunk only removes the duck import and never adds an import for github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/expr/sql, so the identifier is unresolved. Compilation of pkg/expr fails with "undefined: sql" (or a collision if database/sql is imported), breaking the entire build for the expression subsystem.

[BUG] All three DB methods (TablesList, RunCommands, QueryFramesInto) are stubs that return errors.New("not implemented"), and this stub replaces the real go-duck implementation removed from go.mod. Every SQLCommand.Execute and every TablesList call returns "not implemented" at runtime — SQL expression queries that pass the reader gate fail unconditionally in production instead of executing, and no error surfaces until a user runs a query.

[ADVISORY] TablesList builds a json_serialize_sql command and calls RunCommands on a DB whose RunCommands always errors, so the parse-time table extraction path is now dead code. Anyone relying on table extraction for SQL expressions (query validation, variable interpolation) gets a guaranteed error; the surrounding JSON parsing logic at lines 25+ can never execute and will silently rot.

[ADVISORY] The diff removes github.com/scottlepp/go-duck v0.1.0 while keeping pkg/expr/sql/parser.go's NewInMemoryDB resolution dependent on the new local stub, but go.work.sum re-adds go-duck's transitive hashes (thrift, asmfmt, minio/*) implying another workspace module still depends on it. Maintainers running `go mod tidy` in the root module after this lands will see go-duck's indirect requirements reappear/dissappear inconsistently across go.sum and go.work.sum, producing noisy CI dependency-drift failures in the workspace build.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions always returns false, so the QueryTypeSQL branch unconditionally returns the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented". Every SQL-type expression query — regardless of the feature flag state — fails with an error; users with the feature enabled get a broken SQL expression engine, and the flag can never enable anything.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions inverts the flag (returns false when IsEnabledGlobally is true) and then returns false from both branches, making it dead logic that never returns true. The double-negative `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` combined with `if enabled { return false }` means even the intended-on path returns false; the next reader of this code cannot tell whether flag-on or flag-off was meant to enable SQL, guaranteeing future mis-fixes.

[BUG] The replacement NewInMemoryDB returns a DB whose TablesList, RunCommands, and QueryFramesInto are stubs that always return errors.New("not implemented"). SQLCommand.Execute (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:97-101) now always fails: every SQL expression query errors at runtime even past the reader gate — the diff removes the working go-duck implementation and ships no functioning replacement, so the entire SQL expression feature is dead code paths end-to-end.

[BUG] sql_command.go calls sql.NewInMemoryDB() and db.QueryFramesInto without any visible import addition of the new pkg/expr/sql package or local `sql` identifier in the diff context. If the import of the new package is missing (the diff only removes the duck import and rewrites call sites), the package fails to compile with "undefined: sql" — the diff carries no import hunk for pkg/expr/sql.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff covers the new enableSqlExpressions gate or the QueryTypeSQL error return; the diff contains no test-shaped files at all for the new logic. The always-false gate and the not-implemented stubs would have been caught by a single test asserting QueryTypeSQL parses when the flag is on; a future regression in this gate will silently disable or mis-gate SQL expressions again.

[ADVISORY] The gate error message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" leaks an internal implementation state to the API consumer instead of a feature-flag-appropriate message. Frontend users who submit a SQL expression get an opaque "not implemented" error with no hint that it's flag-gated, generating support load and making the failure indistinguishable from a malformed query.

[BUG] NewInMemoryDB returns a stub DB whose TablesList, RunCommands, and QueryFramesInto all unconditionally return errors.New("not implemented"), while the removed go-duck implementation provided working DuckDB-backed behavior. pkg/expr/sql/parser.go TablesList (the SQL expression table-reference parser) and SQLCommand.Execute (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-104) now fail on every invocation, so any user who could previously run SQL expressions gets hard runtime errors — this diff silently removes working functionality rather than adding an analytics framework.

[BUG] enableSqlExpressions has two branches (enabled=true and the fallthrough) that both return false, so the function is a constant false regardless of the feature flag it reads. The featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions toggle passed to it is dead configuration: operators enabling the flag get no effect, and the SQL query type at pkg/expr/reader.go:129-131 is permanently gated behind the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" — the invariant the flag was supposed to enforce (flag-gated enablement) is not enforced by anything.

[BUG] QueryTypeSQL now returns an error 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' before deserializing, contradicting the same package's SQLCommand.Execute path that still attempts to run queries. All frontend SQL expression queries are rejected at read time with a raw error string surfaced to users, while the SQL command execution machinery this diff also modifies remains reachable — the reader and the executor disagree on whether SQL expressions exist.

[ADVISORY] The inverted-flag dead code reads `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` then returns false in both arms, which is textbook untestable dead logic not traceable to any requirement stated in the PR intent. The next developer wiring the flag up must reverse-engineer the intended polarity of IsEnabledGlobally; the local variable suggests a botched condition that will be 'fixed' by deleting the negation and flipping return values without any test to catch a wrong polarity.

[ADVISORY] Dropping github.com/scottlepp/go-duck from go.mod while its replacement (pkg/expr/sql/db.go) is a no-op stub constitutes scope drift: the PR titled 'Advanced SQL Analytics Framework' actually removes the SQL analytics capability. Any consumer of SQL expressions in Grafana regress to errors at runtime; the dependency removal is not traceable to a 'replace with a better framework' requirement since no working replacement exists anywhere in this diff.

[ADVISORY] TablesList builds a SQL command by string interpolation of user-supplied rawSQL into fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL), relying only on doubling single quotes as sanitization. Once the stub NewInMemoryDB is implemented (the whole point of this diff's scaffolding), any SQL expression author can inject arbitrary SQL via quoting edge cases; a staff reviewer is bitten the moment the go-duck replacement lands, because the injection sink is already committed. Currently the stub DB returns 'not implemented' so the sink is inert, which is why this is advisory not blocking.

adjudication.rationale:
In pkg/expr/reader.go, enableSqlExpressions() returns false in all paths:
- It sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`.
- If `enabled` is true, it returns false.
- Otherwise it still returns false.
Therefore enableSqlExpressions() is always false regardless of the feature flag state. Since ReadQuery() (QueryTypeSQL case) returns an error when !enabled, every QueryTypeSQL request will return `sqlExpressions is not implemented` even if FlagSqlExpressions is enabled.
